Title: About Alarm Management
Question: How do I configure About Alarm Management (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Alarm management is concerned with improving the QUALITY of the information within the alarming configuration. This information should be used to reduce the QUANTITY of nuisance alarms (red herrings) so that only the most important and relevant alarms are displayed for your process. In other words, alarm management can counteract inefficient alarming.

Title: About Mitsubishi IEC Developer Connectors

Answer:
Steps: Ensure that the first line of this CSV file contains the following column headings: - Identifier: this specifies the agent name - MIT-Addr: this specifies the scan address - Comment: this specifies the agent description - Remark: this specifies whether the tag should be imported by DBGEN and can specify templates too. - ALL the tags that you want to imported MUST have a '>' or '<' character as the first character of the Remark field. Example of typical headings and an entry: Class,Identifier,MIT-Addr.,IEC-Addr.,Type,Initial,Comment,Remark VAR_GLOBAL,_2400_S01_Step_No,D3423,%MW0.

Title: Agent Server Parameters
Question: How do I troubleshoot Agent Server Parameters (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: Channels: this is the maximum number of possible Client-Server connections from the Agent Server to the outside world, such as to the User Interface, other Agent Servers, DDE links. The default setting is 20. - Remote Timeout: this is the time the system waits before reporting a lost connection between any two Agent Servers, or an Agent Server and the user interface. - Agent Path: this is typically the installation folder in which the Adroit executables and dynamic link libraries are stored. - Save WGP file on exit: check to ensure changes are saved at Agent Server shutdown.

Title: Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Common Status Bits of the Multistate Agent (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
If the MultiState agent goes into an unspecified state (i.e. a combination of inputs which has not been defined), it will be reported as being in State00 and will set the AGENT BAD bit and consequently the BAD bit will be set also. A new MultiState agent that has not been configured and has therefore never known anything except the invalid state will not have its BAD bits set.

Title: OPC Definitions
Topic: - OPC is short for OLE (Object linking embedding) for Process Control, it is a software technology designed, like OLE to allow different applications to exchange data, more specifically allowing an I/O server developed by a 3rd party to communicate to any SCADA. This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. - An OPC Item

It's a technology that allows different applications, such as a 3rd party I/O server and a SCADA system like Adroit, to exchange data. The Recipe Agent executes a step based on its Control Recipe value, checking if it's an end of phase. If not, it proceeds to the next step; otherwise, it performs all verification checks for that phase. Successful verification triggers the phase action, while failure results in stopping execution or performing a configured rollback.

Title: Specific Status Bits of the PID Agent
Topic: Specifications
Question: What are the status bits?
Answer:
The PID Agent uses six status bits to indicate alarm conditions. statusBit16 indicates Low PV is lower than its configured lo alarm value, statusBit17 indicates Low-low PV is lower than its configured loLo alarm value, statusBit18 indicates High PV is higher than its configured hi alarm value, statusBit19 indicates High-high PV is higher than its configured hiHi alarm value. statusBit20 and statusBit21 indicate Ehigh and EHigh-High Error values respectively. The Shift Agent uses status bits to indicate shift end, invalid shift configurations, or an invalid OLEDB connection string.

Title: The Accumulator Agent
Topic: Operation
Question: How do I use Operation (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agent begins a new period immediately when intervalMode is set to 4. Otherwise, it starts a period that ends at the next synchronized period. At the end of each period, the previous value is saved, and a new value is calculated by subtracting the starting value from the input value. A record is added to the history table with period end time, current inputValue, and the value for the period if a SQL Server connection is configured.

Question: How do I use Expression Conditions (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Expression Conditions are defined logical statements that can be used in your expressions. These conditions can include slots and their values, allowing you to create dynamic expressions like 'SUCCESSFUL if the Value slot is greater than 95' or 'SUCCESSFUL if the Open tag is On and the Value slot is greater than 95'.

Topic: Expressions
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Expressions (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
slot value would look something like this: <IOT Name=" SecsInMinute " Description=" The second time value "> <Slots> <Slot Name=" source " Description=" Source of value " Type=" Tagname "> systeminfo.second </Slot> <Slot Name=" value " Description=" Seconds " Type=" Integer "> 0 </Slot> </Slots> <HeaderSlots> </HeaderSlots> </IOT> In the above sample, - the Slot Name " source " defines the tag to which we want to subscribe. - the Slot Name " value " defines the slot where the subscribed tag value will be stored.

Title: The Shift Agent
Question: How do I configure The Shift Agent (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Configured shift patterns are selected using the following order of preference: In other words if one or more shift patterns have the current time configured, then the configuration of the shift pattern determines which is selected, in the following order: - Special non-recurring dates, such as Voting Day 5 Apr 2011. - Annually recurring holidays on a given day of the month, such as Christmas 25 Dec. - Weekly recurring patterns on a given day of the week, such as Sundays.

Title: The Timer Agent
Question: How do I use The Timer Agent (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This agent provides a Boolean value slot as an output, which is enabled (set to TRUE) and disabled (set to FALSE) by the agent, depending upon its current mode of operation. Note: Although does not provide a cold-start value, it does support real-time catch-up on a standby server from a master server, which means that if the master Agent Server fails, the timing operation will seamlessly continue.

- Retrieve row: Use this transaction to update tag/s with value/s from a row of a table in a database, hence a tag-to-field mapping is required. Title: ACK Commands
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for ACK Commands (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Where ' tag ' is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, '[.alarm type]' is optional and allows you to to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance "ANA_1.High" only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas "ANA_1" acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To globally acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format in this globalAck slot: tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type].

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Default Alarm Management Queries (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: - Overloaded > 50% - Reactive 25%-50% - Stable 5%-25% - Robust 1%-5% - Predictive < 1%. Priority distribution: The priority distribution for incidents occurring over a period of time. Typically this should be 5% high priority alarms (>Normal priority), 15% medium priority alarms (=Normal priority) and 80% low priority alarms (<Normal priority). Intermittent incidents: The incidents that activate and deactivate within 10 seconds.

Title: PID Alarm Limits
Topic: Limitations
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Limitations (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit .

Title: The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is disabled
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is Disabled (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
The specified backup path is the root path under which the folders containing the individual backups are stored. Each backup is contained within a folder, named by the date and time at which it was made. Within each backup folder the following sub folders could be present, depending upon which backup options were selected: - The data folder contains the Adroit data files, in the specified compressed format. - The events folder contains the Event logs, in the specified compressed format. - The reg folder contains the Adroit registry files.

Title: The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is enabled
Question: How do I use The Backup Directory Structure when Overwrite is Enabled (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When overwrite is enabled, the backup directory structure includes the data folder (containing Adroit data files), the events folder (containing event logs), the reg folder (containing Adroit registry files), and the sys folder (containing Adroit installation files). Files within these folders will be overwritten if they match files being backed up.

Title: Creating and using the Scan Configuration Report
Topic: Configuration
Question: How do I configure Configuration (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Configuration option allows you to generate a Scan Configuration Report. This report is created by running the Adrcomms.exe command from the Adroit installation folder, specifying the computer agent server name and adding the '/report' parameter. The resulting report is saved as a CSV file at C:\temp\adrcomms report.csv. The agent can be configured by modifying its value slot, including mimicking a value. If the index is valid, the specified string is altered; otherwise, the new string is added to the list at the specified index position.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: How to add additional processes to be monitored
Question: How do I configure add additional processes to be monitored (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
You can add additional Processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service by modifying the HealthMonitorConfig.xml file located in the Health Monitor Service's installation folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Common\Health Monitor). To add a process, such as Notepad.exe, add the following within the </NewDataSet> tag: `<Executables> <Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable> <CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent> <PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit> <PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent> </Executables>`.

Title: Adroit Logging Factor
Question: How do I configure Adroit Logging Factor (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world. Therefore the log file created by Adroit was deliberately engineered to always be 20% of the expected size, since Adroit only stores data when it in physically changes.

Title: Data Logging Compression Methods
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Data Logging Compression Methods (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value.

Title: DisableOnQualityChangeLogging
Question: How do I configure DisableOnQualityChangeLogging (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The `DisableOnQualityChangeLogging` setting, when set to 1 in the registry, prevents DBLog agents from logging on quality change specifically for the "Log on change" logging method. This can be achieved by adding the value `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]\[SOFTWARE]\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[DBLog]` and setting its DWORD value to 1.

Title: Account Policy
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Account Policy (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
A locked account remains locked until an administrator unlocks it or a specified amount of time passes. Locked accounts cannot log on. The also determines whether or not a remote user will be forcibly disconnected from all connections to servers in the domain if that user's logon hours expire, and whether users must log on before changing their passwords. The Windows based controls how passwords must be used by all user accounts. It defines such things as the maximum password age, minimum password age, minimum password length, and whether or not a password history is maintained.

Title: Adding the slots we're interested in
Question: How do I configure Adding the slots we're interested in (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?

Title: Automatic master mode assignment
Topic: An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when:
Question: How do I use An automatic election for master mode at a healthy standby server will occur when: (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
An automatic election for master mode occurs when a healthy master server is removed, becomes unhealthy, or when the serverMode slot of a standby server is set to master or a master server is set to standby. The Adroit system then ensures the previous master is relegated to standby, preventing multiple master servers from existing in the cluster.

Title: Creating IOT Expressions
Topic: Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot
Question: How do I use Creating an IOT agent using expressions in the XML slot (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To create an IOT agent with expressions, define the agent's XML slot structure, specifying the types of input values (x, y, z) and then create an expression slot. The expression slot uses functions like `slot()` to access values from the slots and can include conditional statements like `status16 = slot(z) > 100` to perform calculations and set status values.

Title: Creating the Requests collection
Question: How do I configure Creating the Requests collection (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
One of the objects exposed by the Data Object is the Requests collection, a collection of individual descriptions for required real-time data. The slot names are gathered into another collection called the Properties collection. Since the Data Object provides the Requests collection as one of its properties, the VBA code to gain access to the Requests collection is simply: Set reqs = dataObj.Requests A single request consists of the tag plus the names of all slots to be monitored.

Title: Glossary
Topic: @scan (pronounced at-scan), which is a method of linking the value of one tag to another, by scanning the required tag value directly. active the monitored condition of this incident (alarm/event) is still in effect and has not yet returned to its normal operating state. agent an instance of an agent type, that stores data and typically provides the ability to operate or act on this data. agent group an agent that facilitates the logical grouping of other agents. For example, an AgentGroup agent could contain all agents related to a specific section of a plant, or all agents required for a specific report. alarm the process of monitoring an agent for the occurrence of a specific abnormal condition or state (alarm type). alarm type a named (abnormal) condition or state of an agent that is defined by which of its status bits are simultaneously ON or OFF, which can also list the slots of this agent to report when this condition occurs. alarming strategy a set of guidelines or a plan to optimise the configuration of the alarming of agents. Once created it can easily be transferred and adapted for other projects, as required. aspect ratio a ratio or comparison of its width to its height. The screen resolution determines the aspect ratio of a monitor. More than one screen resolution can have the SAME aspect ratio e.g. the following screen resolutions 800×600, 1024×768 and 1280×960 all share the SAME aspect ratio of 4

Title: Golden Rules for Scanning
Question: How do I use Golden Rules for Scanning (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Golden Rules for Scanning provide guidance on how to scan data effectively. Specifically, always scan the rawValue instead of the value slot, particularly when dealing with Analogs. Furthermore, avoid scanning signed values into Marshal or Multistate agents, and prioritize scanning device addresses ending in "I" or "L".

Title: Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server
Question: How do I use Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Historical Data Catch Up mirrors historical data from the master server to a newly added standby server, focusing on data collected while the standby server was offline. This intelligent mirroring is performed by the SystemDataLog agent (systemDl) to synchronize system time, and is limited to catching up data between two specified date/times for performance reasons.
Category: Classic UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help

Title: Historical Data Management
Topic: Extracting Logged Data
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Extracting Logged Data (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Adroit uses a data extraction facility called Extract that retrieves information from an AgentGroup consisting of DataLog agents, or from a single DataLog agent, for a specified time period. The data is then converted into a CSV (comma separated value) file format that can be opened by a third party application such as Microsoft Excel and formatted to create reports.

Title: How Maximum Demand is Calculated
Topic: Maximum demand calculation example:
Question: How do I use Maximum demand calculation example: (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Maximum demand is calculated by summing the peak power consumption during a 30-minute period. In the example provided, Adroit calculates the maximum demand as ((800*5) + (200*5) + (400*10) + (800*8) + (1500*2)) / 30 = 613.33 kVA. The predicted maximum demand for each episode is also provided, and the MaxDemand status bit would be set if the configured maximum demand limit is exceeded.
Category: Classic UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: help
Keywords: adroit scada, adroit, scada, 800, 200, 400, 1500, 613, classic, other, maximum, demand

Title: How to use Wanlink
Question: How do I configure use Wanlink (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Configuration file of each WanClient , must essentially specify how to communicate to the WanServer and which local tags in these remote Agent Servers (AS3), (AS4) need to be "linked" to tags that reside in the primary Agent Server (AS1) and the communication settings to its WanServer connected to the primary Agent Server (AS1). The WanServer will then establish connection to the primary computer's Agent Server (AS1) and communication based on this configuration will commence from then on.

Title: Improved Integrity
Question: How do I use Improved Integrity (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Improved Integrity ensures data logging functionality in Adroit works correctly. If you configure a tag to log data, you must save the server database afterward to avoid Datalog agent exceptions. The Agent Server always honors data log settings from the agent database (WGP) file, so unsaved configurations will be lost.

Title: IPEnableHeartbeat
Question: How do I troubleshoot IPEnableHeartbeat (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
If you want the Agent Server to monitor that each connection remains healthy and to close unhealthy connections, then implement the following registry setting on the Agent Server computer: This setting enables the Agent Server to monitor the PINGs it received from each client and to also specify the required timeout value, in seconds, where if a PING has not been received within this time period then the connection to this client is deemed unhealthy and this connection (channel) is closed by the Agent Server.

Title: Issues related to using Remote Desktop to Run Adroit
Topic: Problems running the Agent Server
Question: How do I use Problems running the Agent Server (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
You cannot start the Agent Server as an application by using the Windows Remote Desktop (a terminal client). This is because Windows does not support USB ports when you use the Remote Desktop application, so any USB HASP is effectively invisible to the Agent Server. Note: This is not a problem when starting the Agent Server as a service from within a Remote Desktop.

Method Join(AgentName, GroupName : string) : boolean; This method joins an agent to an agent group. If the agent group does not exist, it is created. Parameters: - AgentName - the name of the agent who is required to join a group. - GroupName - the name (AgentGroup) of the group to be joined. Returns: If the call is successful the function returns TRUE else it returns FALSE.

Question: How do I configure Launching Wanlink Components (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:

This setting can also be overridden with the /p:nnnn command-line parameter. If the /persist command-line parameter is used the /p:nnnnn value will be saved to the registry.

Title: Reversing Input Slot Order
Question: How do I use Reversing Input Slot Order (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Reversing Input Slot Order allows you to read the 16-bit input rawValue into Boolean input slots V01-V16 in reverse order, with V01 becoming the Least Significant Bit. This is typically done to accommodate external constraints. To achieve this, set the Registry Key ReverseMultiStateBits to 0 (FALSE) for the WG.INI file.

Title: Routing to Audio Devices
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Routing to Audio Devices (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker.

Title: Secondary Port Disabled
Question: How do I use Secondary Port Disabled (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
A device enters recovery mode when a Read or Write transaction fails, triggering a three-step process: the driver requests an update from the front-end device, times out if there's no response, and retries the request a configured number of times. If all retries fail, the scanning process immediately resumes.

Title: Secondary Port Enabled
Question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Enabled (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Adroit can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails.

Title: Type List CSV File Format
Question: How do I use Type List CSV File Format (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. The rows in this CSV file are sorted alphabetically and the alarm type name is used as an index, so that the first alarm type name has an index of 0.

All NASA provide support for multi channels although this feature is off by default. Title: WanClient Contents
Topic: About WanClient
Question: How do I use About WanClient (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The WanClient application initiates communications to one or more WanServer applications to fetch or send values of Adroit tags that occur in the Agent Server that is also running on the WanClient computer. Therefore, the WanClient creates and maintains a tag link database that stores a list of WanServer(s), that this WanClient is required to connect to, and a list of the tags whose values are communicated to each of the Agent Servers residing on these WanServer computers.

Title: Wanlink Components
Question: How do I use Wanlink Components (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Wanlink allows data to be replicated over a slow or Wide Area Network (WAN) from one Agent Server to another. In other words, it allows remote Agent Servers to behave as if they were normal remote nodes on a Local Area Network (LAN). For further details, see General Description . Wanlink is essentially comprised of the following two components: - WanServer , which allows Adroit tags (agent.slot) within the Agent Server that is also running on the same computer, to be communicated to one or more remote WanClients, which are typically situated across a WAN (wide area network).

Title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for maximum demand and why should you monitor it? (Classic Ui)?
Answer:
Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh.

Therefore if the computer fails then the soft license will no longer work. Your product license can either be a HASP and a soft license, each of which have the following important differences: - A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk. - A Soft license is bound to a specific computer and therefore cannot be transferred to another computer.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: How to add additional processes to be monitored
Question: How do I configure add additional processes to be monitored (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
You can add additional processes to be monitored by the Health Monitor Service by modifying the HealthMonitorConfig.xml file, located in the Health Monitor Service's installation folder (typically C:\[Your Company]\[Health Monitor]\%). To add a process, like Notepad.exe, add the following within the </NewDataSet> line: `<Executables><Executable>Notepad.exe</Executable><CPUCoreThresholdPercent>2</CPUCoreThresholdPercent><PrivateBytesLimit>1146880000</PrivateBytesLimit><PrivateBytesThresholdPercent>80</PrivateBytesThresholdPercent></Executables>`.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Complex mode and KPI calculation
Question: How do I use Complex mode and KPI calculation (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case: KPI% = (Total for the Shift for input1/Run time)/Target KPI If the Input type 2 field (the type2 slot) is NOT set to Unused (0), then the OEE agent is said to be in complex mode.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Running time
Question: How do I use Running time (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This causes the measurement variable (the input1 slot) to remain static or go to zero i.e. inactive. If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the and will raise a downtime alarm status. As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the .

Title: Managing Subscription Queue Length
Question: How do I configure Managing Subscription Queue Length (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Subscription Manager queue length can be adjusted to prevent overfilling. This is done by modifying registry settings within HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Workgroup\wg.ini. Specifically, you can set the 'LocalmemAsyncBufsize' and 'LocalmemHighWaterMark' DWORD values to 2000000 and 1000000 respectively.

Windows can track selected activities of users, by auditing security events and then placing entries in a computer's security log. Title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
Question: How do I use Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don't want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset.
Category: Classic UI - Security
Document Type: help
Section Type: general

Title: Control Bits (user modifiable)
Question: How do I use Control Bits (user modifiable) (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Control Bits fan-out, which means that a slot control bit becomes set or reset, whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits.

Title: To Disable the Task Manager for the Current User
Topic: Disabling the Task Manager for the Current User
Question: How do I use Disabling the Task Manager for the Current User (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To disable the Task Manager for the current user, create a REG_DWORD value named "DisableTaskMgr" under HKEY_CURRENT_USER extbackslash Software extbackslash Microsoft extbackslash Windows extbackslash CurrentVersion extbackslash Policies extbackslash System and set its value to 1. This change will immediately disable the Task Manager for that user.

Title: User Rights Policy

Answer:
The Windows manages the rights granted to groups and user accounts. A right authorises a user to perform certain actions on the system. A user who logs on to an account to which the appropriate rights have been granted can carry out the corresponding actions. When a user does not have appropriate rights, Windows blocks attempts to carry out those actions.

Title: To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service
Topic: How to set up To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service
Question: How do I configure To install or uninstall the Agent Server as a service (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Typically the Agent Server is configured to run as a Service during the install, although you can do this after the install if necessary by using the following command line switches that the Agent Server process (as.exe) provides: - Press the Windows key + R shortcut to open the Run dialog. - Type in as.exe followed by following commands and press ENTER: /install /u:"[Domain\]Username" /p:"Password" /quiet This command will install the Agent Server as a service. The /quiet parameter suppresses any feedback messages. /uninstall This command will remove the Agent Server as a service.

Title: TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem
Topic: TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure
Question: How do I troubleshoot TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure (Classic Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: - Backup your database (WGP file) - Unscan all the tags to that PLC. - Save and restart the Agent Server. - Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each.

Title: New Adroit Scanning Architecture (NASA) ver 1
Topic: saving communications bandwidth.
Question: How do I troubleshoot saving communications bandwidth. in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Continuous polling: The scanning sub-system continues to poll for data even if it is not required. The only current work-around is to create a separate device agent for each plant segment, and scan those tags from it. Then, when the data is not required, stop the device agent. This situation is quite complex, and as a system grows with time, the benefits of this type of configuration are typically eroded by people placing more un-necessary tags on mimics, which causes these scan tasks to run again when only 1 item is needed.

Title: Spectrum Tele-RANGER
Topic: configuration challenges
Question: How do I configure configuration challenges in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Delayed response. With PLC systems a read request is honoured immediately, whereas with a radio telemetry system, several different requests can be sent out before a response to the first one is received. Also, the sequence in which responses arrive is totally unpredictable Exception-based. Instead of using a poll-response type protocol like most other Adroit protocol drivers, the teleRanger driver operates in an exception- or event-based mode.

Title: Adroit Installation Read Me

Answer:
By default both the install and the .bat file used to create the OPCUA certificates run the following two commands to force the system to favour IP4 over IP6 when resolving its addresses: netsh interface ipv6 set prefix ::/96 60 3 AND netsh interface ipv6 set prefix ::ffff:0:0/96 55 4 If after running these commands manually via an elevated command prompt you are STILL unable to enumerate endpoints on a local OPC UA server, which may occur when your computer has multiple network cards, then phone support to resolve this issue.

Title: About Agent Data (Slots)
Question: How do I use About Agent Data (Slots) (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Each agent (instance of an agent type) maintains its own unique set of data and is referred to by its own unique agent name. For details, see About Agents or Naming Agents . Title: About Alarm Acknowledgement
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for About Alarm Acknowledgement (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
For details about acknowledging alarms using the Alarm List Viewer window, see Acknowledging Alarms. Note: To define how the alarming subsystem treats current alarms if an agent's statusalarmInhibit slot is set to one and the agent is currently in alarm and/or unacknowledged, add and configure the SmartInhibit registry value. Adroit provides the following methods of acknowledging alarms: - Global acknowledgement: This should be used when using a standalone Adroit installation or for those alarms that only one operator needs to be made aware of.

Title: About Alarm Management
Question: How do I configure About Alarm Management (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Alarm management is concerned with improving the QUALITY of the information within the alarming configuration. This information should be used to reduce the QUANTITY of nuisance alarms (red herrings) so that only the most important and relevant alarms are displayed for your process. In other words, alarm management can counteract inefficient alarming. Note: By repeating this process regularly, you will be able to ensure that only relevant alarms are generated thereby improving your alarming system.

Title: Agent Subscriptions
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Agent Subscriptions (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
The concept of a subscription is based on the principle of "listening" for updates from a specific Agent tag (or slot). - The process of subscribing is setting up the "listener", by registering with the underlying mechanism of the relevant agent tag. - Other traditional mechanisms usually rely on explicitly reading a data point to update a value, where as subscriptions allow the change to be sent asynchronously to any "listeners". - The result is that the subscription mechanism is more responsive and less redundant so that only actual changes are sent and only when the change occurs.
Category: Smart UI - Agents
Document Type: help

Title: Alarming Agents
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Alarming Agents (Smart Ui)?

Slot Name Type Function bit00 - bit31 BOOLEAN The default slot names representing the I/O bits of the AREC agent. Title: Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents
Question: How do I use Basic Principles of DbAccess Agents (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Each DbAccess Agent represents a transaction on a row, in a table, in a database. Before any transactions can take place, a connection to a database has to be established and a table in this database has to be identified, that requires or contains the information necessary for a transaction. IMPORTANT: If you are connecting to a database across the network and your Agent Server is running as a service, then ensure that the user profile that the Agent Server service uses to log onto the computer HAS the necessary rights to browse the network and connect to the remote database.

Title: How to use the ICMP agent to ensure the availability of a networked device
Topic: In the SmartUI Designer:
Question: How do I use In the SmartUI Designer: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- The STRING pingStatus slot provides a textual description of the status of the last ICMP message used to contact the device, as follows: OK from [IP Address] if it succeeded; Retries exhausted when retrying to contact the device (a timeout failure) and Host unreachable from [IP Address] if it is not possible to contact the device. - The BOOLEAN pingNow slot performs an immediate ping. Note: If the specified timeout is too short then you will never get a "host unreachable" error because the network will not have the necessary time to respond.

Question: What are the key specifications or limits for OLE Server Interface (MISSRVR) API for Agent Servers (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
This OLE Server Interface Specification forms the standard API (Application Programming Interface) for Agent Servers. It effectively defines a contract, by means of which third party client applications can interact in a rich variety of ways with standalone or distributed Adroit configurations. Because OLE is a programming-language-independent standard, third party applications can be written in any OLE enabled development environment, such as Visual Basic™, (VBA) Visual Basic for Applications™ , Borland Delphi™, PowerBuilder™, C++, etc.

Title: OPC Definitions
Topic: - OPC is short for OLE (Object linking embedding) for Process Control, it is a software technology designed, like OLE to allow different applications to exchange data, more specifically allowing an I/O server developed by a 3rd party to communicate to any SCADA. This allows a SCADA Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition, used to monitor and control an industrial plant or process and its related equipment. such as Adroit to use the same I/O server as any other SCADA, eliminating the need for each SCADA to have its own or I/O server for a device. The technology allows for an OPC item ( scan point a scan point licence that is consumed from your Adroit license when information is being manipulated. ) to be read by a SCADA and, if enabled to do so, to also write to the OPC item. - An OPC Item

Title: Order of Execution of a Step of a Recipe Agent
Question: How do I use Order of Execution of a Step of a Recipe Agent (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Recipe Agent executes steps in a defined order. First, it sets the ingredients based on the Control Recipe. Next, it checks if the step is an End of Phase; if not, it proceeds to the next step. If the step *is* an End of Phase, it performs verification checks, and if successful, proceeds with the phase action.

Title: SIMPDRV - Adroit Simulation Protocol Driver
Topic: Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values:
Question: How do I use Automatically Incrementing Scanned SIMPLC Values: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To simulate a dynamic situation, the values in memory are automatically incremented, for every scan, by the DB number. The formula is: newvalue = oldvalue + DBnumber In other words, DB 0 will NEVER increment, and if DB100:DW### is scanned, the value will be incremented by 100 each scan. For Digital tags, the value will TOGGLE.

Title: Specific Status Bits of the PID Agent
Topic: Specifications
Question: What are the specific status bits related to PV alarms?
Answer:
The PID Agent utilizes six status bits to indicate alarm conditions. Specifically, statusBit16 indicates low PV below its configured low alarm value, statusBit17 indicates low-low PV below its configured loLo alarm value, statusBit18 indicates high PV above its configured hi alarm value, statusBit19 indicates high-high PV above its configured hiHi alarm value, statusBit20 indicates Ehigh Error above its eHi alarm value, and statusBit21 indicates EHigh-High Error above its eHiHi alarm value. The Marshal Agent uses 16 status bits to store the value state of each component digital agent.

Question: How do I use Operation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Accumulator Agent operates by immediately starting a new period when intervalMode is set to 4. It then calculates a new value at the end of each period by subtracting the startValue from the inputValue, saving this lastValue. If a SQL Server connection is configured, the agent also adds a record to the history table with the period end time, value, and current inputValue.

Title: The Accumulator Agent
Topic: Trigger event
Question: How do I use Trigger event (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When a occurs: - The agent subtracts the previous interval input value from the current input value to determine the value differential for the current period. - This results in a value which represents "the total production for the last hour or shift or day and so-on" . - It then calculates the rate of change in value, which is the differential value for the current period divided by the interval of this period (value per hour) .

FailPulse Also known as StatusBit19 A short pulse is generated on a transaction failure. - This slot will be set on [1] for a very short period (approximately 100 ms) , if the last transaction failed. Succeeded Also known as StatusBit20 This slot will be set on [1] if the last transaction succeeded. - Will be reset immediately prior to a transaction being executed. However, this slot will automatically be set on [1] if the agent is enabled and the agent is able to reconnect to the database.

Title: The DumpConfig Agent
Topic: How it works
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for How it works (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
When the agent is enabled, the agent will wait for one of three events to happen before performing a snapshot: - The occurrence of the next hourly period. - The very first period is synchronised to midnight, meaning that if you specify an hourly interval of 8, the first snapshot will occur at 08h00 or 16hoo or at 00h00, whichever occurs first. - After that, the snapshot will occur every subsequent 8 hours. - A manual snapshot can be requested via the dumpNow slot - A non-zero value trigger event of a selected trigger tag, when one is specified.

Title: The Frame Agent
Question: How do I use The Frame Agent (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
A Frame agent can store 32 character strings (in slots V01 to V32 ), each string having a length of up to 79 characters (this length excludes the mandatory zero terminator character). These character strings are indexed (from 1 to 32) and the current string being pointed to by the Index is duplicated in the Value field. If the value in FRA01.index slot is 4, then the character string hot will be duplicated in the FRA01.value slot.

Question: What are the key specifications or limits for The ICMP or PING Agent (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
By continuously polling the specified remote IP address, this agent is therefore able to identify potential network problems as they occur by generating alarms when errors are obtained when attempting to contact the specified remote IP address and/or when the round trip time exceeds specified High and High-high times. uses the Internet Control Message Protocol to determine the existence of a remote device on the network. Any IP network device is able to send, receive and process ICMP messages. These messages are only used for troubleshooting network problems and not to transfer data.

Title: Troubleshooting Clustered Agent Servers
Topic: Networking:
Question: How do I use Networking: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Use the PING command to determine if your clustered Agent Server computers are networked correctly. For instance, in the command prompt, type the following: ping -l 64000 -t partnerServerComputerName If you have a low success rate (many packets being lost or a high round trip time), then your network is the problem, which requires input and action from your I.T. department.

Title: Using Analog Agent Alarm Limits
Topic: Limitations
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Limitations (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
- The Low (the lo slot) and High (the hi slot) inner alarm limits are the first warning that a process value has moved outside its acceptable range, and implies that corrective action must be taken as soon as possible. - The Low-low (the loLo slot) and High-high (the hiHi slot) outer alarms are the second warning that the process value has moved further from its acceptable range and reached the second alarm limit.

Title: ACK Commands
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for ACK Commands (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Where ' tag ' is the name of the agent a user wants to acknowledge, '[.alarm type]' is optional and allows you to to acknowledge a specific alarm for the specified agent. For instance "ANA_1.High" only acknowledges ANA_1.High, whereas "ANA_1" acknowledges ALL the alarms relating to the agent ANA_1. To globally acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format in this globalAck slot: tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.alarm type]. To acknowledge more than one alarm at a time, use the following format: ack,tag[.alarm type],…, tag[.

Title: AcknowledgeAtStartup
Question: How do I configure AcknowledgeAtStartup (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This registry value, if set to 1, forces the Agent Server to automatically acknowledge alarms at startup. WARNING: We do NOT RECOMMEND that you set this registry value to 0, otherwise you will be left with unacknowledged alarms as saved in the WGP file which could have occurred a long time ago and, if so, will no longer be relevant.

Title: Alarm Types
Question: How do I configure Alarm Types (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
An alarm is triggered when one or more of the status mask bits in an alarm type of an Alarm agent matches any status bits in the agent being monitored. For an agent to be monitored, you have to apply one or more to the agent (see Alarming an Agent ). The creation of is discussed here. are defined on a per Agent Type basis, which are pre-configured in the postload Adroit database file . Each Alarm Type must be edited to define the alarm triggers that take the form of a descriptive abbreviation, e.g. "Overheating" for Analog agent types, or "Tripped" for Digital agent types.

Title: Alarming strategy
Topic: About Alarming Strategies
Question: How do I troubleshoot About Alarming Strategies (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: Filtering of Alarms: An alarm priority can be specified for each agent, so that alarm agents can filter out all the alarms generated by low priority agents, if necessary. However, since this alarm priority is tag-specific rather than alarm-specific, it cannot be used as an efficient alarm filtering mechanism, for instance if we only want to display a sub-set of the alarms configured for an agent. The only mechanism in Adroit that can achieve this is to use an Alarm list as a destination and use the alarm viewer filtering mechanism.

Title: Automatic WGP File Backups
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Automatic WGP File Backups (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
For details, see Creating Backup Procedures . Note1: These backup files will be created in the folder in which the WGP file resides, EACH time it is saved, regardless as to whether its contents have been changed or not. Note2: Restoring these saved WGP files is still a manual process, which requires: stopping the Agent Server, renaming the WGP file that is currently being used; locating and renaming the required backup file to this name and restarting the Agent Server. The names of these automatically created backup copies, adhere to the following format: name.yyyymmdd_hhmmss_v_n.

Title: Default Alarm Management Queries
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Default Alarm Management Queries (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
This is a measurement of alarm overload on operators, as follows: - Overloaded > 50% - Reactive 25%-50% - Stable 5%-25% - Robust 1%-5% - Predictive < 1%. Priority distribution: The priority distribution for incidents occurring over a period of time. Typically this should be 5% high priority alarms (>Normal priority), 15% medium priority alarms (=Normal priority) and 80% low priority alarms (<Normal priority). The 20 of these alarms can account for almost 50% of total alarm generation.
Category: Smart UI - Alarming

Title: Effective Alarm Characteristics
Question: How do I use Effective Alarm Characteristics (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- Diagnostic: identifies the problem that has occurred. - Advisory: indicates the action that is to be taken. - Focusing: draws attention to the most important issues. While the AlarmManagement agent can ensure that the first four characteristics are met, the last 4 characteristics are supported within the Classic UI by assigning a document to each incident that is accessible from the alarm viewer. The characteristic of an effective alarm is that it should be: - Relevant: requiring acknowledgment and corrective action i.e. NOT an event that can simply be ignored.

Title: FireEventsFromMainThreadOnly ActiveX Property
Question: How do I use FireEventsFromMainThreadOnly ActiveX Property (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Connection Functionality . Property FireEventsFromMainThreadOnly : boolean; This property is used to instruct the object to post a message back to the main thread and fire events from there rather than firing events directly from a secondary thread such as an Adroit subscription manager. This is usually essential in VB6-created containers but not necessary when using the object in VC++ created containers.

Title: PID Alarm Limits
Topic: Limitations
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Limitations (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Note: that whenever the LL alarm is on, the L alarm must by definition already be on. Similarly, whenever the HH alarm limit is reached, the H alarm limit will already have been passed. The alarm will not be cleared until the process value goes past the limit. When the value of the PValue or Error slot of the agent reaches one or more of these configured limits, the agent will set the relevant specific status bit . The PID agent type provides alarming capabilities for both the PV (process value) and the %Error or the percentage deviation of the PV from the SP (the required set-point).

Title: AlarmManagement Database Tables
Question: How do I use AlarmManagement Database Tables (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- Adr_AM_AssociatedValues: This table stores the values of the tags that are associated with each incident. Each tag associated with an incident is stored as a separate record in this table. This table has the following fields (columns): - Idx: The Key field, which is a unique, automatically incrementing number. - IncidentIdx: The unique incident index value of the associated incident record, which is an Idx value in either the Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents or Adr_AM_CurrentIncidents table. - Tag: The name of the tag associated with the incident specified by IncidentIdx .

The Adroit database or .WGP file stores almost all of the data and configuration of the Agent Server, including the added agents, their values and their alarming, logging and scanning configuration. Title: Common Device Configuration
Topic: Primary and secondary parameters
Question: How do I troubleshoot Primary and secondary parameters (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Each device contains that define the available connection channels (or routes) and parameters. The secondary information is optional and is used in the event of a failure on the primary connection, or vice versa. How this secondary port works is simple, if the driver is using the primary configuration parameters and the communication fails, the driver will switch over to (and re-initialise) the secondary port and continue communicating via it if possible.

Title: Connecting the Portal Web Service to a remote Server
Topic: To connect the Web service to a remote Server computer:
Question: How do I configure To connect the Web service to a remote Server computer: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: Navigate to the SmartUI Web Service installation folder, which is typically: C:\Program Files\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI\Webservice . - Locate the "Web.config" file in this folder and open it in a text editor, such as Notepad. Its first four lines should appear as follows: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?> <configuration> <appSettings> <add key="server" value="localhost" /> - Modify the "localhost", so that the value refers to either the network name of the remote Server computer or its IP address. - Save this file and close it. .

Title: Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe
Question: How do I troubleshoot Phase Actions and Tag/Value of a Master Recipe (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: A VARIABLE action will alter recipe execution based on the value of the agent.slot given in the Tag/Value field, as follows: Slot value Action 0 Wait until the slot value changes to a value between 1 and 6 and then perform the action associated with this number 1 Go to next step 2 Go to previous step 3 Go to first step 4 Go to last step 5 Perform verification failure rollback 6 Stop recipe execution Note: the Tag/Value for a VARIABLE action is usually an expression or a slot that returns a Boolean value. The Tag/Value field may also be an explicit number between 0 and 6.

Title: The Configuration SystemInformation Page
Topic: Parameters on startup
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Parameters on startup (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
These parameters should be configured in Adroit Setup (Config) BEFORE the Agent Server is started. - startMaxChannels : This specifies the maximum number channels used by this Agent Server. A channel is a Client-Server connection from the Agent Server to the outside world, such as to the User Interface, other Agent Servers, DDE links. This project name must not be longer than 8 characters, nor contain any embedded spaces. When more than one project name is being used on the same network, ensure that the first 3 characters are unique. - startName : This specifies the name of this Agent Server.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: How to adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for adjust the default thresholds of the monitored processes (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
The configuration file is called HealthMonitorConfig.xml In this file, each specified executable allows you to specify the following thresholds, which specify the normal usage values, which if they are consistently exceeded indicates that there may be a problem and hence the Health Monitor Service will log messages in these instances: - CPUCoreThresholdPercent : This specifies the maximum percentage of the CPU that this process executable should consistently use in normal operation, above which the Health Monitor Service will provide alerts.

Title: Working with the Health Monitor Service
Topic: What does it do?
Question: How do I use What does it do? (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The following CPU usages are checked for each process: - If the CPU % is higher than 50% of 1 CPU Core it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. - If the Memory (Private Bytes) is more than 80% of 1146880000 bytes it gets flagged for higher resolution monitoring. When a Process has been flagged for higher resolution monitoring, then it is checked every 10 seconds: - If the process is still above the thresholds, an event entry is written to the Eventlog indicating the Process ID, Name, Description, Running Time, CPU Usage, Private Bytes & Virtual Bytes.

Title: Adroit Logging Factor
Question: How do I configure Adroit Logging Factor (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When Adroit logging was originally developed in 1992 a design criteria was accepted which has come to prove problematic for some installations in the real world. Up until 1992 the generally accepted default practice was for users to datalog all points at 1 second. However, due to CPU, HDD speeds and serial protocol speeds, the fastest data could only logged at 4-5 seconds.

Answer:
This registry value, if set to 1, this disables: - all the automatic validity checking of alarm values against engineering range that usually occur within the Analog agent, so that its alarm limits can be communicated and therefore configured externally, such as from a front-end device. For instance, one such internal validity check always ensures that the specified HighHigh alarm limit is always greater than High alarm limit, which may not be the case if the new High alarm limit has not been communicated yet.

Title: Data Logging Compression Methods
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Data Logging Compression Methods (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Logging values is an event-based function, by default, a value is logged whenever it changes. When logging values, you can specify both a time and value deadband (in the Datalog agent) to reduce the number of records that you log for a value which effectively 'compresses' your log files so you are able to store more data on the same storage medium. - Using the Value deadband: Values are ONLY logged if their change in value EXCEEDS the specified deadband value. Hence when the value of a logged point does not exceed the previously logged value by more than the deadband, the value is not logged.
Category: Smart UI - Logging
Document Type: help
Section Type: spec

Title: DisableOnQualityChangeLogging
Question: How do I configure DisableOnQualityChangeLogging (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The `DisableOnQualityChangeLogging` setting, when set to 1 in the registry, prevents DBLog agents from logging on quality change specifically for the "Log on change" logging method. This can be achieved by modifying the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\[Wow6432Node]\[SOFTWARE]\[Adroit Technologies]\[Adroit]\[DBLog]` registry value to 1.

Title: Extracting Logged Data
Topic: Examples

For instance the following command, will extract the last 744 hours (31 days) from the groupname of datalogs "EXTRACT_GROUP", using the Date agent "DATA_MONTHLY", on the computer "USER", with the Agent Server name "agl": extract USER.agl,EXTRACT_GROUP,744:0:0:0,0,0,DATA_MONTHLY.asciiTime The latest file retrieved will be saved with the .CSV file extension, and the previous file will become the backup file, and saved as a .BAK. Title: Active Clusters Foundation
Topic: Clustering Agent Servers
Question: How do I configure Clustering Agent Servers (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Clustered Agent Servers, previously known as hot standby, provide both client and server redundancy enabling high availability of the system. Typically, redundancy can be applied to all the levels within the plant. For more details on addressing the important issues that affect the operation and configuration of clustered Adroit Agent Servers, see Important Points to consider when . The general idea of clustering is that the master server services all the I/O and client tasks, while the standby server replicates the master server.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: Adding your own Queries
Topic: Other things you can do:
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Other things you can do: (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
For instance, this %t constraint is used by the "Most frequent alarms (count by type)" query, as follows: SELECT (%t) Incident, Count(Idx) AS [Count] FROM Adr_AM_HistoricalIncidents WHERE dt > ''%b'' AND dt < ''%e'' GROUP BY Incident ORDER BY Count DESC - From (%b) and/or To (%e): These constraints allow your users to specify the time period during which the required incidents occur. This time period in seconds is 1 by default. - Average alarm duration (%ALD). This time period in seconds is 60 by default. - Average acknowledgement duration (%AKD). This time period in seconds is 10 by default.

- Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front-end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured. Using the same PC port / resource, but different PLC ports / resources. Adroit can make use of a different PLC addressing to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component.

Title: AutoConnect ActiveX Property
Question: How do I use AutoConnect ActiveX Property (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The AutoConnect ActiveX property is a boolean setting that instructs an object to automatically connect to a server or track a master node. When set to TRUE, the object will connect to the server defined in the Server property or the master node in the Cluster property, automatically tracking the master node in cluster operation. The ConnectionUpdate callback method is invoked before switching to a new master node.

Title: Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Basic principles of server mode assignment strategies in Adroit (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
The state of a cluster server is recorded in the systeminfo.serverMode (0, 1, 2 = master, standby, normal respectively) and systeminfo.serverState (0, 1 = unhealthy, healthy respectively) slots for every cluster server. A new cluster server always starts up as a standby server. The serverstate slot always starts up as healthy and remains as such unless the user changes it to unhealthy (0) via a script, expression agent or a similar means.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help

Title: Best Practices
Topic: Project Directory Structure
Question: How do I configure Project Directory Structure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Adroit Software should be separated from the configured project(s), since this allows for easier backups, upgrades etc. For this reason, a directory for Adroit projects should be created at the root drive (or wherever the data files are required to be stored), typically called ' C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Configurations\Default ', this project folder should contain the following directories: - \CSV, which should contain all your exported data. - \CustomAgents, which contains all the custom agents created for the project.

Title: Catch-up
Question: How do I use Catch-up (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When a new server is added to the cluster, it must become a mirror image of the active member of the cluster. The new server must restore its historical data (historical ) that it lost during the down time. This historical synchronization or Datalog is facilitated by a new agent called the SystemDatalog agent .

Title: Communication Hardware and Cluster Server I/O Modes
Question: How do I use Communication Hardware and Cluster Server I/O Modes (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Communication Hardware Cluster Server I/O modes define how devices connect and communicate. These modes include parallel scanning, shadowing, and network configurations, each with specific use cases. Parallel and shadowing modes are point-to-point, typically using RS232C, while network modes allow multiple masters to participate simultaneously, such as with L2 bus or Ethernet networks.

POW(2,3) = 8 LN: returns the natural logarithm of the value LN(Slot1) LOG: returns the base-10 logarithm of the value LOG(Slot1) LOGN(Base, value): returns the log Base of the value LOGN(10, 100) = 2 ABS: returns the absolute value ABS(Slot1) SIGN: returns the sign of the value SIGN(Slot1) returns -1 if Slot1<0; +1 if Slot1>0, 0 if Slot1=0 TRUNC: discards the fractional part of the value TRUNC(-3.2) is -3, TRUNC(3.2) is 3 CEIL: returns the value rounded up, away from zero CEIL(-3.2) = -3, CEIL(3.2) = 4 FLOOR: returns the value rounded down, toward zero FLOOR(-3.2) = -4, FLOOR(3.

Title: Creating IOT Expressions
Topic: Expressions using status slots
Question: How do I use Expressions using status slots (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Expressions can utilize named status slots, like 'hi', allowing you to refer to them using either the status nn numbering convention (e.g., status16) or the named status(slotname) convention (e.g., status(hi)). You can use these slots on the right-hand side of an expression, such as status17 = if(status(enabled), slot(abc) > 100).

Title: Date Format Flag
Question: How do I use Date Format Flag (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Date Format Flag, denoted by '#', can be used to prefix formatting code characters after the '%' symbol. When used with %#c, it produces a long date and time representation appropriate for the current locale, such as "Tuesday, March 16, 1993, 12:41:29". When used with %#x, it generates a long date representation appropriate to the current locale, such as "Tuesday, March 16, 1993".

Title: Demand Scanning
Topic: What is demand scanning and how should it be used?
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for demand scanning and how should it be used? (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Note: There is a fair amount of overhead involved for each demand scanned process value, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. Therefore due to this implicit overhead only configure process values to be demand scanned that will benefit from , in other words, do not configure process values for that will NEVER make use of this mechanism (e.g. those that are logged or alarmed).

Title: Desubscribe ActiveX Method
Question: How do I use Desubscribe ActiveX Method (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The Desubscribe method removes a subscription from a previously subscribed tag. It takes a SubscriptionHandle as input, which was previously returned by the Subscribe or SubscribeBulk methods. The method returns TRUE on success and FALSE if an error occurs, with LastError/LastErrorNum providing details about the failure.

Title: Golden Rules for Scanning
Question: How do I use Golden Rules for Scanning (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Golden Rules for Scanning are designed to ensure accurate data retrieval. Specifically, scan the rawValue not the value slot, particularly for Analogs, and avoid scanning signed values into Marshal or Multistate agents. Additionally, scan device addresses ending in "I" or "L" at a speed appropriate for the task.

Title: Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server
Question: How do I use Historical Data Catch Up of the Newly Added Standby Server (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Historical Data Catch Up ensures a newly added standby server receives the historical data from the master server. This intelligent mirroring only copies data from the period the standby server was unavailable, and it's performed by the SystemDataLog agent (systemDl) to catch up data between two specified date/times for performance reasons.

Title: How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy
Question: How do I use How MAPS implements the S88 / S95 hierarchy (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- The Site level is the MAPS project. So you will have one MAPS project per site. For example, XYZ Foods. - The Area level is the defined Plant area/s of the MAPS project. For example, Batching Plant. - The Process Cell level is the PLC/s of each defined plant area. For example, BATCHING PLC. - The Unit level is the collection/s of equipment items within each PLC. - The Equipment module and the Control module levels are NOT separately implemented because this is not supported by the PLC programming architecture.

Title: How Maximum Demand is Calculated
Topic: Maximum demand calculation example:
Question: How do I use Maximum demand calculation example: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Maximum demand is calculated by summing the peak power consumption during a specified period. In the example, Adroit calculates the maximum demand for a 30-minute period by summing the kVA values of each episode, resulting in 613.33 kVA. The predicted maximum demand for each episode is also provided.

Title: How to cluster Servers
Topic: Notes
Question: How do I configure How to cluster Servers (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This is configured by the ClientPingInterval setting of the SmartUI Operator, which is grouped under the ConnectionSettings in the SmartUI Operator.exe.config file. The ClientPingInterval setting determines how often the SmartUI Operator will query the Server for an active connection and its configuration has the following effect upon the performance of the Operator: - If this interval is too frequent interval, this will increase client-server chatter and use up bandwidth unnecessarily. The INITIAL connection for the SmartUI Operator MUST have a running SmartUI Server.

Title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks
Topic: Caching:
Question: How do I troubleshoot Caching: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Caching can optimise the transfer of data between the CLIENT and the SERVER. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. There are TWO main caching techniques, both of which are configured on the CLIENT: - Using the DataElementCachingEnabled setting : This method determines whether the SERVER contains a more recent version of an object than the CLIENT: - If it does, the CLIENT cache will be updated.

Title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks
Topic: Requirements
Question: How do I use Requirements (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To optimize performance for remote clients over slow networks, ensure your computer meets the minimum specifications: a Pentium IV processor with 512MB of RAM, and a bandwidth of 512KB/sec. Additionally, install the latest version of SmartUI and launch both the SmartUI Server and SmartUI Designer for login.

Title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks
Topic: STEP 1: Update the local cache of all your projects
Question: How do I configure STEP 1: Update the local cache of all your projects (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: Open the SmartUI Designer; - Right click on the project that should be cached and select "Update Local Cache"; Note : This may take a while but wait for the message box to appear once the operation is complete. This updates the CACHE files in the Caching sub-folder of the SmartUI ProgramData folder (typically C:\ProgramData\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\SmartUI \Caching) with the latest versions of all the forms of the selected projects. This Caching subfolder can now be transferred to all your SmartUI Operators.

Question: How do I configure STEP 3: Setting up the SmartUI WebService (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:

Title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks
Topic: Subscribe-Poll
Question: How do I use Subscribe-Poll (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- A communications mechanism that can be used on a LAN/WAN or the Internet. - This mechanism does NOT PUSH any data to the CLIENT, but relies on the CLIENT to POLL for the data. - ALL the changes since the last POLL cycle will be retrieved from the SERVER. - This mechanism attempts to reduce latency by minimising round-trips to the SERVER.

Title: How to optimise performance for remote clients over slow networks
Topic: WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER
Question: How do I use WEBSERVICEDATAPROVIDER (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- An indirect, Web Service (XML) connection to the SERVER via IIS. - Packets are compressed before they are made available to the CLIENT. - The communication to the SERVER is normally via IIS on port 80 and then from IIS to the SERVER on port 9000. - Only the SUBSCRIBE-POLL and POLL mechanisms may be used.

It helps to create items that have meaningful names.

For each piece of equipment there can be up to 3 templates, each providing different levels of complexity or diagnostic information, the names of these templates indicate the provided level of complexity as follows: _B_ (basic), _S_ (standard) or _A_ (advanced). IMPORTANT: The greater the level of complexity provided by a template, the more signals are required for this item of equipment, which therefore increases the number of the required SCADA tags. The third section provides the version of this template e.g. v1_0 stands for version 1.

Answer:
- There cannot be more than one master server in a cluster. Hence making a server master will immediately switch the other server to standby mode. - The serverMode and serverState slots between Agent Servers and within an Agent Server are not replicated. - All other server and client clustering operations will operate as normal given the slot values, irrespective of whether a manual or automatic master mode assignment method is used.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: Manual Master Mode Assignment
Topic: Suggested method of operation
Question: How do I use Suggested method of operation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
As suggested in the above scenarios, start all or part of the cluster servers. Set the desired master server as master through the various means available to set the serverMode slot (one way would be to use the dialog in the options-preferences-connection menu item). The automatically assigned clients switch their connection to the new master server. Start both Agent Servers in the cluster at the same time, and then the server with the lowest alphabetical name (i.e. closest to 'a') will become the master server.

Title: Manually Polling OID Values
Question: How do I use Manually Polling OID Values (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To manually poll ALL the OIDs in the list: this will immediately retrieve the values of all the OIDs in the list and sets their corresponding tags to the new values. Note1: The value of any OID that does NOT have an associated Tag in this list will NOT be returned. Note2: This polling occurs immediately, over and above the normal poll cycle. To manually poll ALL the OIDs in the list that are NOT enabled for automatic polling: this will immediately retrieve that values of all the OIDs in the list that do not have their E fields checked and sets their corresponding tags to the new values.

Title: MarkBadIfWriteFails
Question: How do I configure MarkBadIfWriteFails (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
If you have devices that do not allow writes to certain registers (which causes agents to be scan bad when a write fails) then add the following value and set it to 0, so that the next read will simply overwrite the value that the user wanted to write in the first place: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Scanning\ (REG_)DWORD = 0 to force Adroit to not mark values bad when their write fails.

Title: MarkBadOnStartup
Question: How do I troubleshoot MarkBadOnStartup (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Since the Agent Server does not poll values at startup, you can add the following value and set it to 0 to mark your values healthy on startup and display the values that were last saved in the WGP file: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Adroit Technologies\Adroit\Scanning\ (REG_)DWORD = 0, the default value is 1, which marks values bad on startup as is the default Adroit behaviour.

Title: MultiState Data Model
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for MultiState Data Model (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
This approach, namely having a separate bit dedicated to each state, leads to a smooth integration with the Classic user interface multicolor Behaviour, by allowing a different text, line and/or background color for each discrete state. In addition, these bits can be individually alarmed using existing Adroit alarming mechanisms, which means a wide variety of alarm strategies can be developed. These inputs can originate from any Boolean, Integer, or Real data, but will be converted to Boolean TRUE/FALSE indications on being stored in a MultiState agent.

Title: MultiState Operation
Question: How do I use MultiState Operation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
On reaching a new state, a MultiState agent automatically carries out the following actions: - The new state is recorded as the current state. - The new state's description is recorded as the current state description. - Any outputs in the new state's output-true list are set TRUE. - Any outputs in the new state's output-false list are set FALSE.
