Title: PokeWithTime ActiveX Method
Question: How do I use PokeWithTime ActiveX Method (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Agent Functionality . Method PokeWithTime(Agent, Slot : string; Value : variant; Timestamp : datetime) : boolean; This method changes the historical value of a tag. Note: This can ONLY be used to change PAST values of tags NOT current or future values. However, a value that is the SAME as the previous time sample will NOT be accepted. Parameters: - Agent: the name of the agent or tag (agent.slot) whose value is to be changed. - Slot: the name of the slot whose value is to be changed. This parameter is ignored if the Agent parameter contains a tag. - Value: the required value.
Category: Smart UI - Other

Title: Read or Write Scanning Strategy

Question: How do I use Operation of strategy: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
- When the Agent Server is started, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). - When a device stops or starts, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). - When the communications have been restored after a device has failed, the Agent Server receives the values of these scanned tags from the front-end devices (PLCs). - If a value of one of these scanned tags is changed in the Agent Server, this value is written to the front-end device (PLC).

Title: Replication
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Replication (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
All these sources of change are replicated to all Agent Servers in the cluster in order to maintain the mirror image state of the clustered servers. Two instances of configuring within a cluster are: - Client Runtime Transaction Shadowing : All transactions initiated by a client on a server are shadowed to the other server in the cluster to provide total data . - Parallel scanning : Each cluster server is configured to replicate the scanning tasks to provide scan task , that is, each server performs scanning as if it were a normal server.

Title: Reversing Input Slot Order
Question: How do I use Reversing Input Slot Order (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Reversing Input Slot Order is necessary when reading 16-bit input rawValue into Boolean input slots V01-V16, ensuring V01 is the Least Significant Bit. This is achieved by setting the Registry Key ReverseMultiStateBits to FALSE (0) for WG.INI, which reverses the default behavior of having V01 as the Most Significant Bit.

Title: Route List CSV File Format
Question: How do I configure Route List CSV File Format (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm routes that have been configured. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx- ROUTLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. This file consists of the following columns, from left to right: - Alarm-list: The name of the alarm-list agent (multiple list-agents are separated by spaces). - Route number: The route number. - Audio device: The tag.slot name of the agent(s) used to sound the alarms of this alarm route.

Title: Routing to Audio Devices
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Routing to Audio Devices (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Routing an alarm to an audio device has the effect of incrementing or decrementing the specified slot that must be of type boolean or integer. New alarms cause the slot value to be incremented, and acknowledgment of these alarms will cause the value to be decremented. If the start slot of the Beeper agent is used, it will activate a repetitive beeping sound in the PC speaker. The sound pitch will become higher each time the start slot is incremented by a new alarm, and will be lowered when an alarm is acknowledged and the slot decremented.

Title: Secondary Port Disabled
Question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Disabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This failure is a 3 step process: - Adroit requests an update from the front-end device. - Timeout Phase: the request is sent to the front end device, and times out or gives an invalid response. - Retry Phase: Step 2 is repeated for the number of retries configured.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: procedural
Keywords: adroit scada, adroit, port, troubleshoot, scada, failure, timeout, retry, smart, other, secondary, disabled

Title: Secondary Port Enabled
Question: How do I troubleshoot Secondary Port Enabled (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Adroit can make use of a secondary port to cater for the possible failure of some communications hardware component. For this to be effective, the hardware used by the secondary port should be totally separate (e.g. extra serial card and cable). A device goes into recovery whenever a Read or Write transaction fails. This involves a port switchover, and only occurs once in any transaction. The driver then runs through Steps 2 and 3 using the secondary port.
Category: Smart UI - Other
Document Type: help
Section Type: procedural
Keywords: adroit scada, adroit, port, troubleshoot, scada, failure, serial, driver, smart, other, secondary, enabled

Title: Time Stamping
Question: How do I use Time Stamping (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
When the agent subsequently sends a subscription update to another agent, or picture element Behaviour, the same timestamp value is passed on. For example, if the Alarm agent receives a subscription update, it will route the timestamp it gets to whichever printers, event logs, alarm lists and beeper agents it has been configured with. Adroit achieves its accuracy by data at the point of creation whenever possible. Scanned values get their timestamp from the data packet returned by the front-end device, if the protocol driver is exception based and implements a time-stamping protocol.

Title: Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance
Question: How do I use Title 21 CFR Part 11 Compliance (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Title 21 CFR Part 11 (21 CFR 11) of the Code of Federal Regulations deals with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines on electronic records and electronic signatures (ERES). This defines the criteria and circumstances under which electronic records and electronic signatures are considered to be trustworthy, reliable and equivalent to paper records by the FDA.

Title: Type List CSV File Format
Question: How do I use Type List CSV File Format (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This file is created when an Alarm agent is exported to store its alarm types that have been created. The filename adheres to the following naming convention: xxxxx-TYPLST.CSV, where xxxxx represents the name of this Alarm agent. The rows in this CSV file are sorted alphabetically and the alarm type name is used as an index, so that the first alarm type name has an index of 0. - Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. - Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set. - Bit-mask: A bit-mask of the relevant header bits that are set.

Question: How do I troubleshoot Usage scenarios NOT recommended for demand scanning: (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Steps: Demand scanning cannot be used as a strategy to "reuse" your scan points, since as explained above a scanned point license is not relinquished by a demand scanned tag when its tag is not being scanned, since the NASA driver has to constantly query the Agent Server to determine when this process value is being used. - We do also NOT recommend the use of demand scanning for a clustered Agent Server that uses shadow scanning and a proxy server to handle requests for its tags from remote clients. Since this could return INCORRECT VALUEs.

Title: Updating cached graphic forms
Question: How do I use Updating cached graphic forms (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
By default, each SmartUI Client refers to either the Designer or the Operator, both of which are client applications of the Server. caches the data that it requests from the SmartUI Server to improve its response time. For instance, if a graphic form that has been cached is opened by the Client, this graphic form is loaded from the local cache instead of retrieving it from the Server via the Internet/LAN so it opens quickly. In other words, no further design changes have been made to this graphic form that is stored on the Server.

Title: Using Pseudonyms and Macros
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Using Pseudonyms and Macros (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
For details, see Enabling Pseudonyms and Macros . Note1: Pseudonyms and macros are specific to the Command agent in which they are defined and are not global to all Command agents. However when a Command agent is copied, any defined macros and pseudonyms will also be duplicated. Title: Value formatting syntax
Question: How do I use Value formatting syntax (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
{0:e} = 1.420000e+000 {1:E3} = -1.240E+004 F or f Fixed point The resultant string is of the form "-ddd.ddd..." where each 'd' indicates a digit (0-9). The string starts with a minus sign if the number is negative. Note: If the precision specifier is omitted, the default numeric precision is used. {0:f4} = 1.4200 {1:F} = -12400.00 G or g General The number is converted to the most compact of either fixed-point or scientific notation, depending on the type of the number and whether a precision specifier is present. {0:N} = 1.42 {1:n3} = -12,400. {0:N} = 1.42 {1:n3} = -12,400. {0:N} = 1.

Title: What is maximum demand and why should you monitor it?
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for maximum demand and why should you monitor it? (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Maximum demand is an additional cost for most non-domestic power users. It is the method used by your electricity provider to control how much electricity you use, especially at peak times, when your usage coincides with peak domestic usage. Your maximum demand limit is the maximum amount of electricity that you are allowed to use to run your process during peak demand times, which in South Africa is measured in kVAh. Consequently monitoring your maximum demand can result in considerable savings and reduced power usage.

Document Type: help

Title: Working with 21 CFR 11 mode
Topic: Enabling 21 CFR 11 mode:
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Enabling 21 CFR 11 mode: (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Note: When running an Adroit Agent Server and a SmartUI Server on two separate computers, BOTH computers must be configured for 21 CFR 11 mode using the SAME password. This password is encrypted and stored in the configuration (.config) files on the SmartUI Server computer. Since 21 CFR 11 requires that system access be limited to authorised individuals, access to these configuration files need to be limited through the use of directory and file level security. For details, see Working with Configurations . For details, see Working with Configurations .

Title: Working with 21 CFR 11 mode
Topic: Requirements
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Requirements (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
The configuration (.config) files on the SmartUI Server computer must be made inaccessible (through directory and file level security) to prevent unauthorised users from: - disabling the 21 CFR 11 setting thereby "turning off" the audit mechanism entirely and the use of the secure connection to the Adroit Agent Server and - deleting the mandatory local secure SQL Server Compact database that stores the 21 CFR 11 auditing.

Topic: What 21 CFR 11 mode enforces (design-restrictions):
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for What 21 CFR 11 mode enforces (design-restrictions): (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
21 CFR 11 compliance requires limiting system access to authorised individuals. Therefore the connection to the Adroit Agent Server is now secured to limit exactly which client connection to it is allowed to prevent unsanctioned access (from Classic or legacy Adroit Clients and third party applications). These recorded (logged) changes include: the timestamp of the change; the change made; the initiating user and, if applicable the authorizing user, and a computed hash of all these fields to detect tampering.

Title: Working with connections
Topic: Connections are created are follows:
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Connections are created are follows: (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Each connection consists of the following mandatory properties, apart from the user login details: - Host Name: The network name or IP address of the Server computer that will be connected to. Note: If this Server uses a port other than 9000 (the default), this becomes: 'HostName:PortNumber'. - Type: The physical connection between this Client computer and the required Server computer i.e. via the LAN or the Internet. - Mode: The method of communicating data between the Client and Server computers, which depends upon the selected Type .

Title: Working with the Adtech Licensing Utility
Topic: Important differences between a HASP and a soft license:
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Important differences between a HASP and a soft license: (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Your product license can either be a HASP and a soft license, each of which have the following important differences: - A HASP license is bound to a USB HASP, which has a specific serial number - this is therefore portable and not restricted to a specific computer, but has associated security risks and needs to be insured at your own risk. - A Soft license is bound to a specific computer and therefore cannot be transferred to another computer.

Topic: Examples of expressions . An expression can be thought of as a collection of terms associated by mathematical operators, which are evaluated in a strict order of precedence. Mathematical Operators . Mathematical Functions . This order can be overridden by using brackets. Each term of the expression is composed of primary elements, which can either be signed (or complemented) numbers or variables (v1 to v20, and v99 which is equivalent to "value"), or sub-expressions. This recursive definition of an expression means that expressions can be nested to any level of complexity. Note

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Available time
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Available time (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
Whereas KPI calculations are performed against runtime, OEE calculations are calculated against the time that the process/machine is available for production. The OEE agent therefore uses the BOOLEAN available slot (or the optional BOOLEAN tag reference availableTag ) to determine the maximum . - This slot should be ON when the machine/process is supposed to be running. - If the process/machine is under maintenance or operators are at lunch/tea, this slot should be OFF.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Calculation duration
Question: What are the key specifications or limits for Calculation duration (Smart Ui)?
Answer:
By default, the agent records the OEE or KPI based on shift numbers, which are determined by the Shift agent specified by the Shift tag field of the edit dialog ( shiftAgent slot). For details, see Configuring the Shift agent . At the end of each shift the OEE or KPI is recorded and automatically reset for the start of the next shift. If you want to use the agent for recording the OEE or KPI on a "per batch" basis, then: - Disable the autoReset slot of the agent (uncheck the Shift auto-reset checkbox of the edit dialog) and - Programmatically reset the agent at the end of every batch.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Complex mode and KPI calculation
Question: How do I use Complex mode and KPI calculation (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
To allow for KPIs that have one measurement divided by another measurement (other than time), such as kWh/ton- the OEE agent supports a second measurement input slot ( input2 ). For normal OEE and KPI calculations, input2 is not used and the input type is set to Unused (0), by default. In this case the input1 slot is divided by time.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: OEE calculations
Question: How do I use OEE calculations (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The OEE agent performs using the following formula: OEE% = Quality% * Performance% * Availability% Where: Quality% = Quality factor(%) * ((Total for the Shift - Reject Count)/Total for the Shift) Performance% = Total for the Shift/(Design capacity (per hour) * Run time) Availability (hours)% = Run time/Available time Availability Percent of scheduled production (to measure reliability) or calendar hours 24/7/365 (to measure equipment utilization), that equipment is available for production.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Quality factor
Question: How do I use Quality factor (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Quality can be calculated in many ways, depending on the type of process and the variables/information available to calculate quality. Therefore, the OEE agent calculates the quality using the reject and total counts for the shift, which is multiplied by an external , expressed as a percentage. This % value (the qualityFactor slot) is the external whose value (0 to 100) must be driven externally.

Title: Factors affecting OEE or KPI calculations
Topic: Running time
Question: How do I use Running time (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
This causes the measurement variable (the input1 slot) to remain static or go to zero i.e. inactive. If the measurement variable (the input1 slot) remains inactive for a configurable amount of time then the OEE agent will stop incrementing the and will raise a downtime alarm status. As long as the input1 slot is changing AND is not zero, the agent assumes that the process/machine is active and increments the . KPI calculations are performed against runtime.

Title: SubscriptionUpdate ActiveX Event
Question: How do I use SubscriptionUpdate ActiveX Event (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Agent Functionality . Event SubscriptionUpdate(ClientHandle, UpdateType, Status : integer; Value : variant) ; This event or callback method informs the client of a change in the value of a subscribed tag. Parameters: - ClientHandle: a client handle as passed in the call to Subscribe/SubscribeBulk. - UpdateType: 0 - Normal subscription update 1 - Agent/slot status change subscription update 2 - Server disconnected subscription update - Status: the status of the agent. - Value: the value of the tag (only valid for normal subscription update).

Note: R restricted security access can only be assigned to non-global groups and users. For these reasons, it is recommended that: - careful consideration be given to which users and groups are given global security access to a Server.

Title: Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user)
Question: How do I use Condition Bits (not directly modifiable by the user) (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Because the agent bit might have been set by the user or system - and we don't want to lose this information - all agent condition bit values are derived by combining slot condition bits with the agent condition bits. For this purpose, the agent status retains a raw and a derived status word. If an agent bit is therefore set before one of its slot bit are set, it would still remain set when all slot bits are reset. Condition Bits fan-in, which means that an agent condition bit is automatically set to 1 whenever one of the corresponding slot condition bits is set to 1.
Category: Smart UI - Security
Document Type: help
Section Type: general
Keywords: adroit scada, adroit, scada, smart, security, condition, bits, not, directly, modifiable, user, help

Title: Control Bits (user modifiable)
Question: How do I use Control Bits (user modifiable) (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Control Bits fan-out, which means that a slot control bit becomes set or reset, whenever the corresponding agent control bit is set or reset. Note: Unlike Condition Bit fan-in, Control Bit fan-out does not use positive logic (nor negative logic, for that matter): when an agent bit is set or reset this action is performed on all its corresponding slot bits. Therefore if a slot control bit is already set when the agent control bit is reset, then this slot control bit will not be restored to its set state but will remain reset along with all the other corresponding slot bits. Global Inhibit .

Title: Philosophy for End User Applications
Question: How do I use Philosophy for End User Applications (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
The general philosophy is for the user to create an instance of a coarse grained object, and then instruct the object to create many finer grained objects inside itself. A coarse grained object corresponds to a connection to a known Agent Server, either running on the same computer as the application, or some other computer on a local- or wide-area network.

Answer:
When I run the Agent Server, the message "Error load completion agent [BOILER1]." appears. Although no driver or hardware configuration was changed, there is no longer any communication. A: Make sure the mouse is plugged into the correct port. If the mouse is on the port the driver would use, the mouse will work but the Adroit driver will not. Q: When writing to a register, the value does not change, why? Title: TroubleShooting an Intermittent Communication Problem
Topic: TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure
Question: How do I troubleshoot TroubleShooting Driver Communication Failure (Smart Ui) in Adroit SCADA?
Answer:
Determine which request is causing the communication failure. If the driver fails once and then succeeds on the retry, then the fault lies within the PLC and that this is NOT an Adroit problem. But, if the retry also fails then either Adroit has a bug or has been incorrectly configured. Follow the steps below to trouble-shoot the location of the problem: - Backup your database (WGP file) - Unscan all the tags to that PLC. - Save and restart the Agent Server. - Gradually add the scanning back in (in very small groups) waiting about 30 seconds between each.
Category: Smart UI - Troubleshooting
Document Type: help

- xxx timeouts increment when no or too little data has been received on the port in the time allotted for a transaction, resulting in a retry. The following describes all the available counters: - Transactions: The number of successful transactions performed by this device. - Init failures: The number of times this device attempted to initialise or configure the communication hardware and failed. - Retry's: The total count of retries performed on read or write operations. - Percent errors: This is an indication of the communication fault frequency, which is expressed as a percentage.
